item.description: Employers' liability insurance in Singapore answers the claim WICA does not: a court action for negligence, with no statutory cap. Section 63 and MOM's rules.

item.description: Group medical insurance in Singapore is voluntary. What the Employment Act already requires of you, what a group plan covers, and the IRAS 1% and 2% cap.

item.description: A worm in npm packages, an AI-run exploit campaign, a breached email vendor. What a Singapore SME inherits from a supplier's breach, and the 3-day PDPA clock.

item.description: CSA's September alerts say patch now. One published SME cyber proposal form defines neglected software at 45 days. What an unapplied patch does to a claim.

item.title: Compulsory Motor Insurance in Singapore: What the Law Requires for Every Vehicle Your Business Runs
item.description: The minimum legal insurance required to drive on a Singapore road covers injury to other people and nothing else. What the Motor Vehicles Act commands.

item.title: NATAS Membership and Travel Agent Insurance in Singapore: Where the Association Ends and the Law Begins
item.description: NATAS membership is voluntary and is not a licence. What actually governs a Singapore travel agent, and where the insurance duties really come from.

item.title: Restaurant Association of Singapore (RAS) Membership and F&B Insurance
item.description: Restaurant Association membership imposes no insurance on an F&B business. The duties that arrive come from the SFA licence, the lease and the landlord.

item.title: REDAS Membership and Insurance: What Real Estate Developers in Singapore Should Know
item.description: REDAS is a private trade body, not a regulator. It issues no licence and mandates no member cover, so a Singapore developer's duties sit in the contracts.

item.title: SCCCI Membership and Insurance: What the Chinese Chamber Means for SME Cover
item.description: SCCCI is a chamber, not a regulator. It issues no licence and imposes no cover, so a member's real Singapore obligations originate somewhere else.

item.title: Security Association Singapore Membership and the PLRD Insurance Overlap
item.description: Security Association membership is voluntary and buys you no cover. The obligations that bind a security agency come from the PLRD licence instead.

item.title: Singapore Business Federation Membership and Your Insurance Obligations
item.description: SBF membership is statutory for companies above a capital threshold, but it is not an insurance arrangement. What the Act requires and what it does not.

item.title: Singapore Hotel Association Membership and Hospitality Insurance
item.description: Hotel Association membership is voluntary and imposes no insurance. The duties that do reach a hotel come from the licence, the lease and the contracts.

item.title: Singapore Logistics Association Membership and Insurance for Logistics SMEs
item.description: Logistics Association membership is not a licence and imposes no insurance. What does bind a freight forwarder is the trading conditions it signs up to.

item.title: SNEF Membership and the Employer's Insurance Picture in Singapore
item.description: SNEF represents employers inside Singapore's tripartite system. It is not a regulator and imposes no cover, so the employer duties come from elsewhere.

item.title: Spa and Wellness Association Membership and Insurance for Singapore Operators
item.description: Spa association membership in Singapore obliges you to buy nothing. Treatment liability, public liability and work injury cover come from somewhere else.

item.title: Commercial Motor Excess and No-Claim Discount: How Fleet Pricing Actually Works
item.description: Two levers set your Singapore commercial motor premium and most SMEs read both wrong: what the excess actually does, and how NCD behaves across a fleet.

item.title: Cyber Insurance: First-Party vs Third-Party Cover and What Each Pays
item.description: A cyber policy has two halves. First-party pays your own breach costs, third-party pays what you owe others. Which half a Singapore claim falls in decides.

item.title: Equipment Breakdown vs Property All Risks: What Covers SME Machinery
item.description: Property All Risks covers sudden external damage, not a machine that fails from the inside. For Singapore SMEs that inside failure is the whole gap.

item.title: Fidelity Guarantee vs Commercial Crime vs Cyber Crime: Where the Cover Overlaps
item.description: Fidelity, commercial crime and cyber crime all answer dishonesty, which is why Singapore SMEs treat them as one. Where each of the three actually starts.

item.title: Foreign Worker Medical Insurance vs WICA vs Group Health: What Each Actually Covers
item.description: Three covers get confused for one migrant worker and Singapore compels two of them. What foreign worker medical, WICA and group health each actually do.

item.title: Goods-in-Transit vs Motor Cargo vs Marine Cargo: Which Covers Your Delivery Fleet
item.description: Goods in transit, motor cargo and marine cargo pay for different journeys. Which follows your goods out of Singapore, and where each of the three stops.

item.title: Professional Indemnity vs Public Liability: Which Does a Singapore Service Business Need?
item.description: They answer different claims, so most Singapore service businesses need both. Public liability follows injury and damage; PI follows your advice.

item.title: General Average Declared: A Singapore Importer's First 72 Hours
item.description: Cargo sacrificed to save a voyage becomes everyone's bill. What general average means for an importer, and what to do in the first 72 hours.

item.title: Does Your Singapore SME Actually Need D&O Cover? A Decision Guide
item.description: No Singapore law makes D&O compulsory for a private company, so it is a risk decision rather than a compliance one. What the exposure actually looks like.

item.title: Group Health Insurance for a Small Singapore SME: When It Starts to Pay Off
item.description: No Singapore statute requires group health cover. What decides it is hiring, retention and cost, so here is the arithmetic rather than the sales pitch.

item.title: Sole Proprietor vs Pte Ltd: How Your Business Structure Changes Your Insurance
item.description: A sole proprietor and the business are one in Singapore law, so a claim reaches personal assets. Incorporation moves that line, and what cover must do.

item.title: Business Interruption Sum Insured: The Gross-Profit Basis Explained
item.description: Singapore insurers rate business interruption on insurable gross profit, not the figure in your accounts. It is turnover minus only the variable costs.

item.title: Commercial Property and Fire Insurance for Singapore SMEs: The Complete Guide
item.description: No statute forces you to insure your own premises. Your lease and your lender almost certainly do, and their wording decides the sum insured you need.

item.title: Construction Insurance in Singapore: BCA, SCAL, CAR and the Full Picture
item.description: Construction site insurance requirements in Singapore come from three places: your BCA grade, the WSH Act, and the contract. Only one cover is statutory.

item.title: Cyber Insurance for Singapore SMEs: The Complete Guide
item.description: Singapore SMEs: the PDPA and Cybersecurity Act duties that create cyber exposure, what first-party and third-party cyber cover pays, and the silent-cyber gap.

item.title: Foreign Worker Insurance in Singapore: WICA, Medical, and Repatriation, End to End
item.description: Hiring a Work Permit or S Pass holder is not one insurance decision. Several duties start at once under EFMA, and they attach at different moments.

item.title: Professional Indemnity Insurance for Singapore Service Businesses: The Complete Guide
item.description: Professional indemnity insurance in Singapore: who the law requires to hold it, the minimums the statutes set, and the claims-made mechanics that decide it.

item.title: Public Liability Insurance for Singapore SMEs: The Complete Guide
item.description: Public liability insurance in Singapore: no statute makes it compulsory; leases, tenders and venues do. What the clause asks for, and how to evidence it.

item.title: Tenant vs Landlord: Who Insures What Under a Commercial Lease in Singapore
item.description: No Singapore statute divides the insurance burden in a commercial lease. The covenants do, and they decide who insures the building and the fit-out.
